question: Should nix-openclaw add interim README/template guidance for the existing push-mode Gmail hook workaround now, or wait for the upstream pull-delivery stack before changing the public Nix setup path?
rationale: Both paths are plausible: the reporter has a working workaround that fits current config pass-through, but a maintainer already tied the desired long-term fix to cross-repo pull delivery and first-class nix-openclaw integration.

options.title: Document Push Workaround Now
options.body: Add a small README/template example that sets `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey`, constrains Gmail session-key prefixes, and keeps the first-class pull work separate.

options.title: Wait For Pull Stack
options.body: Keep the issue open until the RFC and OpenClaw pull PR land, then document only the new first-class Nix path.

options.title: Close As Upstream-Only
options.body: Treat the upstream OpenClaw docs as sufficient and do not add nix-openclaw-specific Gmail hook guidance.

recommendation.title: Document Push Workaround Now
recommendation.body: Add a small README/template example that sets `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey`, constrains Gmail session-key prefixes, and keeps the first-class pull work separate.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the maintainer already coordinating the RFC, gogcli, OpenClaw, and nix-openclaw direction in the issue thread.
